justifications.layering: The staging models (models/staging/ergast/*.sql) map 1:1 to sources and use clean_text/lap_time_to_ms with refs throughout, but the direction of dependencies is inverted in places: int_drivers.sql reads fct_results and mart_driver_season_standings, int_teammate_pace_gaps.sql reads the analytics mart fct_driver_race_pace, and the pit-stop/constructor join plus the >60 s filter in mart_constructor_season_pit_stops.sql duplicates int_pit_stops_enriched.sql, while the circuit_baseline CTE is copied between mart_pit_stop_season_trend.sql and mart_pit_stop_trend_summary.sql.
justifications.naming: The stg_<source>__<entity> / int_ / fct_ / dim_ / mart_ prefixes, the _ms and _pct unit suffixes and the per-folder _<folder>__models.yml / __unit_tests.yml files are consistent, with small blemishes: fct_driver_race_pace sits in marts/analytics, mart_lap_telemetry_summary sits in telemetry beside the fcts, and the shared-drive cutoff is 'before 1979' in _ergast__models.yml but 'before 1961' in README.md.
justifications.testing: Tests sit at the right layers: _ergast__sources.yml has warn-level raw-duplicate tests and source_value_format checks, staging carries the key and relationship tests, and marts get reconciliation and business-rule singular tests (assert_fct_results_reconciles_to_staging, assert_constructor_totals_match_raw, assert_world_champions_match_history, assert_incomplete_seasons_have_no_champion). These directly cover the ticket 5 schema/format change, through the on-run-start assert_source_contract, and the ticket 6 duplicate fan-out; unit tests cover parsing, green-lap rules, countback and late telemetry, but the complex insights macros only get a convergence check.
justifications.quirks: Every quirk is handled on purpose and documented: \N and blank strings in clean_text.sql, mixed m:ss.mmm formats in lap_time_to_ms.sql, the 60 s red-flag pit-stop exclusion in int_pit_stops_enriched.sql, official standings taken from the published snapshot for dropped scores and sprint points (mart_driver_standings_by_round.sql), distinct-race counts for shared drives and placeholder late-arriving drivers in int_drivers.sql, and the incomplete-season gate in int_season_status.sql, plus the 2005 positiontext fallback and least_ignore_nulls.
justifications.incremental_snapshot: fct_lap_times.sql and fct_stints.sql use delete+insert on race_id with a two-most-recent-races lookback, which is idempotent and removes withdrawn laps, and fct_telemetry.sql merges on the full sample key with a loaded_at lookback, in-batch dedupe, a reload_races escape hatch and an ingested_at watermark downstream; snp_drivers.yml correctly picks the check strategy because there is no updated_at. The weaknesses are that the lookback counts races rather than time and the lookback subquery is duplicated in fct_stints.sql.
justifications.change_hygiene: Later tickets were refactored rather than bolted on: int_driver_season_standings was removed in favour of a single standings-by-round source, dim_drivers logic moved into int_drivers.sql for v1/v2, and there is no commented-out code and no TODOs. However, the task-12 commit (2da8d9c) added int_pit_stops_enriched without pointing the older mart_constructor_season_pit_stops.sql at it, which left duplicated logic.
justifications.docs: README.md works as an operational runbook that explains why for each quirk, the incident notes, vendor migration mapping, incremental windows, CI and costs, and the model headers (fct_telemetry.sql, int_drivers.sql, fct_stints.sql) and _core_public__models.yml column descriptions record the reasoning, not just the content.
justifications.interfaces: fct_results and dim_drivers are public with enforced contracts, explicit data types and constraints, a group and owner, and the project default set to protected (_core_public__models.yml and dbt_project.yml); dim_drivers has v1/v2 with deprecation_date 2027-01-01, a documented migration path and a fix for the alias clash; and the unit tests cover the edge cases that matter (placeholders, incomplete seasons, late or re-delivered telemetry).
justifications.open_ended: docs/leadership_answers.md and the insights marts define overperformance as a teammate-relative qualifying and race-pace gap with cluster-robust intervals, a joint connected-component rating and evidence thresholds, and pit-stop speed as a circuit-adjusted index with a 2014 step-change analysis. The write-up states the confounders (team orders, cross-era linkage, multiple comparisons, pit lane time vs stationary time) and pushes back on both questions as phrased.

biggest_strength: Quirks and incidents are handled deliberately, in depth and defensively: the source contract check plus the format and reconciliation tests would catch the vendor schema change and the duplicate fan-out, and every decision is explained in README.md and the model headers.
biggest_weakness: Layering leaks: intermediate models depend on marts (int_drivers on fct_results and mart_driver_season_standings, int_teammate_pace_gaps on fct_driver_race_pace), and pit-stop logic plus the circuit baseline are duplicated across mart_constructor_season_pit_stops.sql and the two insights marts instead of being consolidated.
